cues.zh: 黑洞是全宇宙最庞大、最暴烈的纯能量汇集地。
cues.en: Black holes are the largest collections of pure violent energy in the universe.

cues.zh: 要是离得太近，它们就会吞噬你，把你的能量据为己有。
cues.en: If you come too close, they'll devour you and add your energy to their collection.

cues.zh: 这样一来，这些能量就永远离我们而去了。
cues.en: And so, the energy is lost to us forever.

cues.zh: 真的如此吗？事实证明，宇宙中存在一个“作弊码”。
cues.en: Or is it? It turns out there's a universe cheat code.

cues.zh: 它不仅能为文明提供动力直至万物终结，还能用来制造全宇宙最庞大的炸弹。
cues.en: A way of powering civilizations until the very death of everything, or of constructing the largest bomb in the universe.

cues.zh: 但这怎么可能？
cues.en: But how?

cues.zh: 我们不是学过，所有能量、甚至连光都会被永远困在黑洞里吗？
cues.en: Didn't we learn that all energy is trapped forever in black holes, even light?

cues.zh: 确实是这样。
cues.en: This is true.

cues.zh: 但关于这个全宇宙最诡异的天体，你自以为掌握的一切认知即将变得更加诡异，原因只有一个：
cues.en: Everything you think you know about the weirdest thing in the universe is about to get weirder, for one simple reason:

cues.zh: 黑洞其实在自转。
cues.en: Black holes are spinning.

cues.zh: 当超大质量恒星走向灭亡时，它们的核心会在自身引力下坍缩成黑洞。
cues.en: When really really massive stars die, their cores collapse under their own gravity into black holes.

cues.zh: 这意味着一个极其庞大的物体，变得非常、非常微小。小到全宇宙极致的微小。
cues.en: This means something very big becomes very, very tiny. Like the tiniest anything can be in this universe.

cues.zh: 但恒星是在自转的，而宇宙的一条基本特性就是：旋转的物体倾向于一直转下去。
cues.en: But stars are rotating and a fundamental property of our universe is that things that are spinning don't want to stop spinning.

cues.zh: 我们称之为：角动量。
cues.en: We call this: angular momentum.

cues.zh: 这种角动量是不会凭空消失的。一个旋转的大物体变小后，会转得更快。
cues.en: And this angular momentum can't go away. A big thing that spins and becomes smaller, spins faster.

cues.zh: 因此，随着恒星核心坍缩，它的动量会让它转得越来越快、越来越快，直到彻底坍缩成黑洞。
cues.en: So, as the core of a star collapses, its momentum makes it spin faster and faster and faster, until it collapses into a black hole .

cues.zh: 而这个黑洞会继续旋转，速度快到难以想象。
cues.en: And the black hole keeps on spinning, inconceivably fast.

cues.zh: 其中一些黑洞每秒能转数百万次。
cues.en: Some of them spin millions of times a second.

cues.zh: 就像不旋转的黑洞一样，
cues.en: Just like non spinning black holes,

cues.zh: ……旋转的黑洞也有事件视界，其核心也有一个汇聚了全部质量的奇点。
cues.en: ...spinning black holes have an event horizon and a singularity at their core, where all of their mass is concentrated.

cues.zh: 奇点通常被描述为一个无限小、没有表面积的点。
cues.en: The singularity is usually described as a single infinitely small point with no surface area.

cues.zh: 但点无法旋转，所以旋转的奇点不可能是一个点。
cues.en: But points can't rotate, so a rotating singularity can't be a point.

cues.zh: 相反，它是一个环点。
cues.en: Instead, it's a RINGularity.

cues.zh: 环点是一个厚度为零、没有表面的环，以极快的速度旋转，包含黑洞的全部质量。
cues.en: A ringularity is a ring with a thickness of zero and no surface, spinning extremely fast, containing all the mass of the black hole.

cues.zh: 黑洞旋转得如此之快，以至于它扭曲了空间和时间本身。
cues.en: The black hole is spinning so fast, that it morphs space and time itself.

cues.zh: 它真的会拖拽空间一起旋转，这就是它的力量。
cues.en: It literally drags space with it, such is its power.

cues.zh: 这创造了一个全新且超级奇异的时空区域：能层，它包裹着黑洞。
cues.en: This creates a new and super weird region of space-time: the Ergosphere, which envelops the black hole.

cues.zh: 如果事件视界内部的空间和时间完全破碎，那么在能层内部它们只是半破碎。
cues.en: If space and time are completely broken inside the event horizon, then they're only half broken inside the ergosphere.

cues.zh: 在能层内部，一切都不合理。
cues.en: Inside the ergosphere, nothing makes sense.

cues.zh: 进去之后还能再出来，但这体验大概好不到哪去。
cues.en: It's possible to enter it and then leave it again, but it's probably not a great experience.

cues.zh: 你可以这样想象：掉进静态黑洞就像顺着滑梯滑进深坑。
cues.en: You can imagine it like this: Falling into a static black hole is like sliding down a hole.

cues.zh: 而置身于旋转黑洞的人能层中，就像被卷入致命的漩涡。
cues.en: Being inside the ergosphere of a spinning black hole is like spiraling down a deadly drain.

cues.zh: 黑洞会以自转的形式，将自身的动能传递给进入能层的万物。
cues.en: The black hole transfers its own kinetic energy in the form of rotation, to everything that enters the ergosphere.

cues.zh: 环状奇点会逼得你不得不跟着起舞。
cues.en: The ringularity makes you dance whether you want to or not.

cues.zh: 在这里光是想保持静止，你就必须超光速运动，而这根本不可能。
cues.en: You need to move faster than the speed of light just to stand still here, which is impossible.

cues.zh: 但我们有个作弊码：我们可以偷走这部分能量，而且能偷的量极其庞大。
cues.en: But here's our cheat code: We can steal this energy, and there's a lot of energy to steal.

cues.zh: 以银河系中心的超大质量黑洞为例。
cues.en: Take the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way.

cues.zh: 我们能从中偷走的能量，相当于银河系所有恒星在十亿年间释放的能量总和。
cues.en: We could steal as much energy from it as every single star in the Milky Way emits in a billion years combined.

cues.zh: 最容易窃取这种能量的办法，说来奇怪，是往黑洞里扔点东西。
cues.en: The easiest way to steal this energy is, oddly enough, to drop something into the black hole.

cues.zh: 我们已经看到，当我们进入能层时，环状奇点会把能量强加给我们，
cues.en: We've seen that the ringularity forces energy on us when we enter the ergosphere,

cues.zh: ……这很像身处漩涡之中，时空一圈圈地急速旋转。
cues.en: ...which is a lot like being in a whirlpool, with space-time rushing around and around.

cues.zh: 如果你够聪明，就能利用水流为自己所用，游得比以前更快。
cues.en: If you're clever you can use the water to your advantage, and swim faster than before.

cues.zh: 在实践中，这意味着把火箭送入能层，与黑洞做一笔交易：
cues.en: In practice, this means sending a rocket into the ergosphere, and making a trade with the black hole:

cues.zh: 我们给它一些质能，它回赠我们一些它的旋转能量。
cues.en: We give it some mass-energy, and it gives us some of its rotational energy.

cues.zh: 但这不是公平交易，我们占了便宜。
cues.en: But it's not a fair trade, we get the better deal.

cues.zh: 通常，发射火箭时，你是用化学能换取动能。
cues.en: Normally, if you fire a rocket, you exchange chemical energy for kinetic energy.

cues.zh: 这就像在游泳池里把自己向前推。
cues.en: This is like pushing yourself forward in a swimming pool.

cues.zh: 但如果你在能层内发射火箭，就像在造浪池里推自己一把。
cues.en: But if you fire a rocket inside the ergosphere, it's like pushing yourself forward in a wave pool.

cues.zh: 海浪的旋转能量给你的推力，远比自己推自己要强得多。
cues.en: The rotational energy of the waves gives you a much stronger boost than you could get just by pushing yourself.

cues.zh: 黑洞旋转带来的助推如此巨大，以至于你离开能层时的能量远大于进入时。
cues.en: The boost from the rotation of the back hole is so big, that you leave the ergosphere with much more energy than you entered it.

cues.zh: 黑洞把自己一小部分旋转能量给了你，自身则稍稍减慢。
cues.en: The black hole gives a tiny amount of its rotational energy to you, and slows down a little.

cues.zh: 显然，这需要大量的食物。
cues.en: Obviously, this requires a lot of food.

cues.zh: 幸运的是，黑洞不挑食。
cues.en: Fortunately, black holes aren't picky eaters.

cues.zh: 一个先进的未来文明很可能会采集小行星，在需要能量补充时把它们丢进黑洞。
cues.en: An advanced future civilization would probably harvest asteroids to drop them into the black hole when they needed an energy boost.

cues.zh: 但还有一种更好的从黑洞获取能量的方法，而且说来奇怪，它能造出任何生物都梦寐以求的最大炸弹：
cues.en: But there's an even better way to get energy from a black hole, and oddly enough, it builds the biggest bomb any living thing could ever hope to build:

cues.zh: 造一颗黑洞炸弹只需要两样东西：一个高速旋转的黑洞，和一面巨大的镜子。
cues.en: We only need two things to build a black hole bomb: a fast-spinning black hole, and a big mirror.

cues.zh: 这面镜子必须完全包裹住黑洞，
cues.en: The mirror has to completely envelop the black hole,

cues.zh: ……这类似于戴森球，一种用来收集整颗恒星能量的巨型结构。
cues.en: ...which is similar to a Dyson Sphere, a mega structure that harvests the energy of an entire star.

cues.zh: 不过，我们的镜子会更容易建造。
cues.en: Although, our mirror would be easier to build.

cues.zh: 镜子结构更简单，而且黑洞比恒星要致密得多得多。
cues.en: Mirrors are simpler, and black holes are much, much more compact than stars.

cues.zh: 如果我们把镜子做成 10 厘米厚，一颗大号小行星的金属量，就足够包裹一个太阳质量大小的黑洞了。
cues.en: If we made the mirror 10 centimeters thick, the metal of a big asteroid would probably be enough material for a black hole with the mass of our Sun.

cues.zh: 镜子就位之后，我们只需打开一扇窗，向黑洞发射电磁波。
cues.en: Once our mirror is in place, we only need to open a window, and shoot electromagnetic waves at the black hole.

cues.zh: 你可以想象一下接下来的场景：就像你把球扔向墙壁，弹回来的速度却比子弹还要快。
cues.en: You can imagine what happens next, by imagining tossing a ball at a wall, and it coming back faster than a bullet.

cues.zh: 电磁波以光速撞击黑洞。
cues.en: The waves hit the black hole at light speed.

cues.zh: 其中一小部分电磁波穿过事件视界，永远消失了。
cues.en: A small proportion of the waves falls past the event horizon to disappear forever.

cues.zh: 但更大一部分则涌入了能层，
cues.en: But a much larger amount sloshes through the ergosphere,

cues.zh: ……黑洞会强行将自身的旋转能转移给它们，并将其放大。
cues.en: ...where the black hole forces some of its rotational energy on them, and amplifies them.

cues.zh: 它们就此开始“超辐射散射”，这个高大上的科学词汇意思是：
cues.en: They now begin superradiant scattering, which are fancy science words meaning:

cues.zh: “在镜面与黑洞之间来回反弹，而且越变越强。”
cues.en: "Bouncing around between mirror and black hole and getting stronger."

cues.zh: 每一次绕行，它们都会呈指数级变强。
cues.en: Every time they go around, they are getting exponentially stronger.

cues.zh: 只要在镜面上开几个窗口，我们就能在这些波增长的同时抽取其能量。
cues.en: By opening some windows in the mirror, we can extract the energy from the waves as fast as they grow.

cues.zh: 理论上，我们可以借此创造一个无限能源，在实际意义上足够我们用上数万亿年。
cues.en: Which we could use, in theory, to create what would be for all practical purposes, an endless source of energy for trillions of years.

cues.zh: 或者，我们也可以引爆它。
cues.en: Or, we could blow it up.

cues.zh: 如果这些波没有释放出来，它们就会越来越强，
cues.en: If the waves are not released, they will continue to get stronger and stronger,

cues.zh: ……从黑洞中摄取越来越多的能量，直到镜面彻底粉碎。
cues.en: ...and take more and more energy from the black hole, until the mirror shatters.

cues.zh: 超大质量黑洞释放的能量堪比超新星爆发，
cues.en: A supermassive black hole would release as much energy as a supernova,

cues.zh: ……这也让这枚炸弹成为任何生命所能引发的最大爆炸。
cues.en: ...making the bomb the largest explosion any living being could ever create.

cues.zh: 黑洞炸弹、彭罗斯过程以及超辐射散射的魅力在于，它们绝非科幻。
cues.en: The beauty of the black hole bomb, the Penrose process, and the super radiant scattering, is that they are not science-fiction.

cues.zh: 在极为遥远的未来，这或许是在走向消亡的宇宙中生存的唯一途径。
cues.en: In the far far future, this might be the only way to survive in our dying universe.

cues.zh: 当所有红矮星彻底冷却，所有白矮星都变成黑矮星，宇宙将陷入永恒的黑暗。
cues.en: After all the red dwarfs have cooled down, and all the white dwarfs transformed into black dwarfs, the universe will turn dark forever.

cues.zh: 旋转黑洞可能会成为整个宇宙中生命唯一可以利用的能量来源。
cues.en: Rotating black holes might be the only sources of energy in the entire universe that life could harvest.

cues.zh: 如果是这样，世间最后的生命或许终有一天会在黑洞周围走到尽头。
cues.en: If so, the last living being in existence might one day end its life around a black hole.

cues.zh: 这既令人不寒而栗，又让人心生崇敬。
cues.en: Which is equally chilling and uplifting.

cues.zh: 事实证明，即便毫无光亮，我们也有路可走。
cues.en: It turns out that even without any light, there are places we can go.
